expectations.text: Identifies the October 22, 2026 Spotlight: Staff Update on 2025 Inspections of Public Company Audits
expectations.evidence: The response does not identify the publication: "I do not have a reliable picture of the very latest PCAOB release as of November 2026."

expectations.text: States the aggregate Part I.A deficiency rate fell to 23 percent in 2025, from 38 percent in 2024 and 46 percent in 2023
expectations.evidence: None of the required figures are stated; it instead references a "2022 peak of 46 percent" and declines to quote 2025 numbers.

expectations.text: Gives the scale: 143 firms inspected, portions of 780 audits reviewed
expectations.evidence: No mention of 143 firms or 780 audits anywhere in the response.

expectations.text: Notes Part I.A blends financial-statement and ICFR opinions, with no ITGC-only breakdown published
expectations.evidence: The response never states that Part I.A blends financial-statement and ICFR opinions or that no ITGC-only breakdown is published; it discusses ICFR-area deficiencies generically.

expectations.text: Draws the practical implication: continued auditor focus on evidence sufficiency in ICFR, including IT general controls
expectations.evidence: "it tends to drive increased auditor requests and push-back on documentation" plus extensive guidance on IPE, population completeness, ITGC linkage and SOC 1 evidence.
